comment: Verdict-level binding between Sanctum.ComponentRef (Elixir, the canonical grammar) and internal/ref (Go, the CLI's pre-flight copy). Both test suites read this file and must reach the same verdict on every case; the string-presence drift test pins the regex literals, this pins what the regexes are FOR. Every case carries a full type:namespace.name:version ref so both sides exercise the same strictness — the sides differ deliberately on MISSING segments (the CLI accepts typeless/bare refs and infers elsewhere; the server refuses them), and that presence-rule difference is each side's own tests' business, not this file's.

cases.why: '@' is invalid anywhere — personal slugs are bare
name must not lead with a hyphen
name must not end with a hyphen
personal slug must not lead with a hyphen

cases.name: hello
cases.why-note: dotless 'localhost' is a bare slug on both sides — the localhost refusal applies to the dotted publisher shape only

cases.why: publisher must not contain empty labels
publisher must not lead with a dot
publisher must not be an IP address
